title: The Three States & Your First Commit

questions.prompt: Which three areas does Git organize your project into?

options.text: The working tree, the staging area, and the repository
The client, the server, and the backup
The draft, the review, and the release
The branch, the tag, and the remote

questions.explanation: You edit files in the working tree, assemble the next commit in the staging area (index), and store permanent snapshots in the repository (.git).

options.text: Permanently records your changes in history
Stages a file's current content for the next commit (and tracks new files)

questions.explanation: git add moves a file's current content into the staging area so it will be part of the next commit. Nothing is in history until you run git commit.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: A commit records whatever is in the staging area
git add stages a file's content at the moment you run it
A brand-new file starts out untracked
git commit automatically uploads to GitHub

questions.explanation: Commits snapshot the staging area, git add captures content at that instant, and new files are untracked until added. Committing is local — sending work to GitHub is a separate git push.

questions.prompt: The command that turns an ordinary folder into a Git repository is: git ______
questions.explanation: git init creates the hidden .git directory, turning the current folder into a repository.

questions.prompt: You run `git add report.txt`, then edit report.txt again, then run `git commit`. What does the commit contain?

options.text: The latest edit you just made
The version as it was when you ran git add

questions.explanation: git add snapshots the file at that moment. The later edit is unstaged, so the commit captures the earlier staged version. You'd need to git add again to include the new edit.

questions.prompt: Match each command to what it does.

pairs.right: Show what is untracked, modified, and staged
Stage changes for the next commit
Record the staged snapshot into history

questions.explanation: init creates the repo, status reports state, add stages, and commit writes the snapshot to the repository.
